```{r}
#Data Setup - Converting to Time Series
library(fpp2)
library(forecast)

TOTALSA <- read.csv("TOTALSA.csv")

TOTALSA$observation_date <- as.Date(
  TOTALSA$observation_date,
  format = "%m/%d/%Y")

TOTALSA_ts <- ts(
  TOTALSA$TOTALSA,
  start = c(1976, 1),
  frequency = 12)

attributes(TOTALSA_ts)
plot(TOTALSA_ts)
Acf(TOTALSA_ts)

# Question 1
## Mean
mean_forecast <- meanf(TOTALSA_ts,12)
plot(mean_forecast)

##Naive
naive_forecast <- naive(TOTALSA_ts,12)
plot(naive_forecast)

##Random Walk
rwf_forecast <- rwf(TOTALSA_ts,12, drift = TRUE)
plot(rwf_forecast)

##Seasonal Naive
snaive_forecast <- snaive(TOTALSA_ts,12)
plot(snaive_forecast)

##Moving Average
MA5_forecast <- ma(TOTALSA_ts, order = 5)
plot(MA5_forecast)

MA9_forecast <- ma(TOTALSA_ts, order = 9)
plot(MA9_forecast)

#Question 2
mean_forecast
naive_forecast
rwf_forecast
snaive_forecast
MA5_forecast
MA9_forecast

#Question 3
plot(TOTALSA_ts,
     main = "TOTALSA Forecast Comparison",
     xlab = "Year",
     ylab = "TOTALSA",
     xlim = c(2000, 2027))
lines(mean_forecast$mean, col="red",lwd = 2)
lines(naive_forecast$mean, col="blue",lwd = 2)
lines(rwf_forecast$mean, col="green",lwd = 2)
lines(snaive_forecast$mean, col="orange",lwd = 2)
lines(MA5_forecast, col="purple",lwd = 2)
lines(MA9_forecast, col="pink", lwd = 2)

#Question 4
train <- window(TOTALSA_ts,
                end = c(2025, 12))

test <- window(TOTALSA_ts,
               start = c(2026, 1))

##Mean
mean_test <- meanf(train, 12)

## Naive
naive_test <- naive(train, 12)

## Random Walk
rwf_test <- rwf(train, 12, drift = TRUE)

## Seasonal Naive
snaive_test <- snaive(train, 12)

##Accuracy
accuracy(mean_test, test)
accuracy(naive_test, test)
accuracy(rwf_test, test)
accuracy(snaive_test, test)

mae_results <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Mean",
            "Naive",
            "Random Walk with Drift",
            "Seasonal Naive"),

## MAE Comparison
MAE = c(
  accuracy(mean_test, test)["Test set", "MAE"],
  accuracy(naive_test, test)["Test set", "MAE"],
  accuracy(rwf_test, test)["Test set", "MAE"],
  accuracy(snaive_test, test)["Test set", "MAE"]))

mae_results

## Model with Lowest MAE
mae_results[which.min(mae_results$MAE),]
```
